prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Evidence is still thin for single-test change kinds (adoption layout, choose_path layout, finish copy, home layout, sign_in incentive, sign_in layout, sign_in redesign).
Redesigning adoption screens (adoption, redesign) and adding hints to the sign-in screen (sign_in, hint) were helpful and delivered winning tests.
Copy revisions on path selection (choose_path, copy) and adding new screens at the finish step (finish, new_screen) consistently hurt performance.
No clear effect was seen for waiting screen changes (home notification, wait_info, redesign, hint) or finish step tweaks (finish hint, finish redesign).
Predictions were generally too high compared to noise-corrected measured outcomes.

Changes:
0: [adoption, redesign] Grid layout redesign for photo upload screen: Redesign the photo upload screen into a structured multi-card grid layout to better guide custom pet photo submission. (why: Adoption has a high mean time of 1017s and users reported custom pet creation failures in support tickets.)
1: [adoption, new_screen] Pet naming step insertion: Insert a dedicated pet naming screen right after custom photo upload to personalize pet setup before generating the adoption certificate. (why: Adoption step takes median 89s / mean 1017s; adding a focused pet naming step breaks up complex photo setup.)
2: [adoption, new_flow] Stage layout redesign for pet pick friend screen: Rebuild the pet selection screen into a stage layout presentation highlighting featured pet avatars. (why: Adoption step takes up to 1017s on average; stage presentation provides high focus for avatar selection.)
3: [finish, redesign] Split layout redesign for home intro screen: Redesign the home intro screen into a split layout presenting desktop placement settings alongside pet activation controls. (why: Finish completion drops to 64.8% and support emails show confusion regarding desktop pet controls.)
4: [choose_path, redesign] Carousel layout redesign for choose path screen: Redesign the path selection screen into a full-width swipeable carousel screen. (why: 16.9% drop-off on choose path; carousel layout offers clear visual distinction between options.)
5: [sign_in, hint] Existing account pet restoration hint on sign-in: Display a hint explaining that signing in restores existing desktop pets and settings. (why: 8 support emails (largest theme) reported pets missing or reset after signing in again.)
6: [home, wait_info] Desktop overlay initialization status hint on waiting screen: Display status updates about desktop overlay initialization and screen rendering during pet setup. (why: Home waiting step has a long mean time (2336s), and 3 support emails reported pets not appearing on desktop.)
7: [home, notification] Desktop pet launch system notification toggle: Add a system notification toggle on the waiting screen so users get notified when pet initialization completes. (why: Waiting step mean time is 2336s; users switch away while waiting and lose context.)
8: [sign_in, incentive] Cloud storage pet memory backup incentive callout: Add a visual badge explaining that sign-in enables cloud backup for pet personality traits and memories. (why: Sign-in drop-off is 17.6% and support received multiple complaints about lost pets upon re-login.)
9: [finish, hint] Desktop pet tray icon and control hint on home intro: Add a hint explaining how to locate and control the pet via system tray and desktop shortcuts on the final screen. (why: Support received 3 emails asking how to control, hide, or interact with the pet post-onboarding.)

scores.note: Adoption redesigns have a proven track record of winning (+3.0% over 9 tests).
Adding new screens tends to increase friction and hurt funnel conversion.
New flow changes lack direct past data, but adoption changes can be effective.
Finish step has highest drop-off, but finish redesigns have shown modest effect (+2.0%).
Choose path redesigns historically yield flat or slightly negative results (-0.1%).
Sign-in hints consistently win (+2.4%) and target the top support complaint.
Addresses high waiting times and support emails, but wait info changes have weak clear effects (+0.7%).
Targets high drop/wait times with moderate past success on notifications (+1.9%).
Strong alignment with sign-in drop-off and support mail, but single-test evidence.
Finish hint showed +2.9% lift across tests, targeting high drop-off at the final step.
